units.text: INT. THE HARGREAVES KITCHEN - NIGHT
Rain against the window, steady and unremarkable.
The fridge hum has died.
Somewhere down the road a transformer has given up, and the whole street has gone the colour of weak tea.
A single candle on the table.
A cold pot of something on the hob.
A mug, a second mug, a phone face-up between them.
ROSALIND HARGREAVES, 50s, cardigan, reading glasses on a string, stands at the sink with her back to the room.
Her son, TOM, 17, sits at the table in a school blazer he has not taken off.
The clock on the wall has stopped at ten past nine.
You're back early.
units.name: ROSALIND
paren: rinsing a cup that is already clean

units.text: Not really.
units.name: TOM
paren: turning the phone over, then back

units.text: Outside, a dog barks twice and thinks better of it.
ON PHONE: "DAD: Spoke to your mum.
We'll sort it.
Don't be daft."
He texted you as well, did he?
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Said not to be daft.
units.name: TOM

units.text: That does sound like him.
units.name: ROSALIND
paren: drying her hands slowly on a tea towel

units.text: The candle gutters.
A gust finds the back door and goes away again.
Neither of them moves to fix it.
I got the letter from Durham.
units.name: TOM
paren: picking at the edge of the table

units.text: Did you.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: They've offered me a place.
units.name: TOM
paren: a breath out through his nose

units.text: Well. That's marvellous.
units.name: ROSALIND
paren: finally turning, the towel in both hands

units.text: You don't sound it.
units.name: TOM

units.text: I'm told it's the done thing, to sound it.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: The rain eases for a moment.
In the quiet, the house ticks as it cools.
This is the last evening the three of them will pretend to be a family under this roof.
I've not even said I'll go yet.
units.name: TOM
paren: standing, the chair scraping the tiles

units.text: You've said it. You said it when you came in with your coat still on.
units.name: ROSALIND
paren: folding the towel, setting it down, squaring its corners

units.text: ON PHONE: "DAD: pick up. please."
Mum, I'm not leaving you here on your own.
units.name: TOM
paren: snatching the phone, thumb over the screen, a crack in his voice

units.text: Thomas. You will go. And I shall be perfectly all right. It's only a power cut.
units.name: ROSALIND
paren: crossing the kitchen, taking the phone from his hand, setting it face-down on the table

units.text: The candle burns on.
Somewhere across the road, a generator coughs and catches, and one lit window blinks into being.
